newsitem.title: UK: Gilts steal weekly government bond prize - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Gilts steal weekly government bond prize - Salomon.

text.p: British gilts stepped out from behind the normally dazzling southern Europeans in the latest week, emerging as the best performing debt market in Salomon's world government bond index.
The gilt market, which notched up a 1.40 percent local currency return, was followed closely by French OATs with a 1.22 percent gain in francs.
Salomon's index as a whole gained 0.52 percent in local currency terms but just 0.09 percent in U.S. dollar terms.
Belgian and Finnish bonds took up joint third place, both gaining 1.18 percent in local currency terms.
All European markets cranked up a positive return in local currency terms as inflation and economic growth remained subdued, keeping interest rates either on hold or forcing them lower.
German Bunds returned 0.84 percent in marks, Spanish Bonos gained 0.95 percent in pesetas and Italian BTPs earned 1.07 percent in lira.

Analysts said the gilt market was helped along in particular by a clutch of data suggesting the economy is weaker than had been feared and news that interest rates are on hold for another month, despite some expectations that another rate rise was on its way this week. U.S. Treasuries, which suffered the damaging impact of a stonger-than-forecast December employment report on the first day of Salomon's week, lost investors 0.19 percent, the only local currency loser in the index.
The U.S. dollar terms, however, Treasuries found company in negative ground, with German, Austrian, Swiss, Danish and Dutch bonds all posting negative returns.
Canadian bonds came up on top in terms of U.S. dollars, gaining 1.28 percent, but the market managed only a 0.38 percent gain in terms of its own currency.

Australian bonds gained 0.34 percent in Aussie dollars, and 0.35 percent in U.S dollars, while Japanese government bonds -- normally one of the index's weaklings -- managed a respectable 0.56 percent gain in for yen investors.

Salomon's bond index is calculated using all government bonds with over one year to maturity, weighted for market capitalisation. Only bonds freely available to institutional investors and with a certain minimum amount outstanding are included. Returns take account of price moves and accrued interest.
